unit: μGy/day (micro-gray per day, absorbed dose in tissue-like detector)
type: Surface absorbed dose rate, galactic cosmic rays (GCR)
location: Gale Crater, Mars surface (-4.4 km MOLA)
measurementPeriod: 7 Aug 2012 - 1 Jun 2013 (~300 sols, near solar maximum)
screenNote: Average galactic cosmic ray dose measured on the rover at Gale (210 ± 40 μGy/day; daily values 180-225). Not inside a spacesuit. Suit shielding and solar storms are not modeled.
sepNote: The only solar particle event RAD saw on the surface in this period (11-12 April 2013) raised the dose rate ~30% and added 0.025 mGy in total. Larger events are possible; no storm scenario is modeled.
